name: Familial Supernumerary Nipples

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnosis of familial supernumerary nipples

criteria.description: Presence of one or more accessory nipples along the embryonic milk line
Positive family history of supernumerary nipples consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
No associated major congenital anomalies or syndromic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of accessory nipples along the milk line with a positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; genetic testing is not routinely performed.

imaging: Ultrasound may reveal absence or presence of accessory mammary gland tissue
Mammography rarely indicated unless malignancy suspected
genetic: Familial inheritance pattern consistent with autosomal dominant transmission
other: Clinical examination is primary diagnostic tool
Histopathology if biopsy performed shows nipple-like structures without glandular tissue

distinguishingFeatures: No familial pattern of accessory nipples
Presence of glandular tissue rather than just nipple

redFlags: Rapid enlargement or change in accessory nipple
Ulceration or bleeding at accessory nipple site
Associated systemic symptoms suggesting syndromic involvement
